edit_from_base: 'a deadzone so small player movements do not move the view' -> 'screen shake on hard landings'
prompt: Add a follow camera with screen shake on hard landings.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Read player.gd and level_01.tscn to learn how the Player moves, how it detects landing (is_on_floor transitions), and what its vertical velocity looks like at impact. Also check the level's bounds so the camera can be limited correctly.
2. Add a Camera2D as a child of the Player so it follows automatically, and enable it as the current camera. Enable position smoothing and tune the zoom for the level's tile size.
3. Set camera limits (left, right, top, bottom) from the level_01 extents or TileMapLayer used rect so the view never shows empty space beyond the level.
4. Create a small camera script (e.g. camera_shake.gd) attached to the Camera2D that exposes a shake method taking an intensity and duration. It applies a decaying random offset each frame and resets to zero when finished.
5. In player.gd, track the downward velocity just before landing and detect the airborne-to-grounded transition. When the impact speed exceeds a tunable hard-landing threshold, call the camera's shake method with intensity scaled to the impact speed.
6. Expose the threshold, max intensity, and duration as exported variables so they can be tuned in the editor without editing logic. Keep normal small hops below the threshold so they cause no shake.
7. Run level_01 and test: walk, jump, short drops, and long falls, confirming smooth follow, no jitter against the tilemap, and shake only on hard landings. Adjust smoothing, threshold, and decay based on feel.
8. Verify the two enemy scenes and any level transitions are unaffected, and that only one Camera2D is active at a time.

1. Open level_01.tscn and player.gd to confirm how the Player moves, where it detects floor contact, and how the level's bounds are laid out. Note the TileMapLayer extents so the camera can be limited to them.
2. Add a Camera2D as a child of the Player so it follows automatically, and enable position smoothing and a small look-ahead for a polished feel. Make it the current camera for the scene.
3. Set the camera limits (left, right, top, bottom) from the level's TileMapLayer used rect so the view never shows empty space past the edges of the level.
4. Attach a small camera script to the Camera2D that exposes a "shake" entry point taking a strength value, and that decays the shake offset over a short duration each frame. Use the camera's offset property so the shake does not fight the follow smoothing.
5. In player.gd, track vertical velocity while airborne and record the peak fall speed. On the frame the Player transitions from airborne to on-floor, compare that speed against a tunable hard-landing threshold.
6. When the threshold is exceeded, call the camera's shake with a strength scaled by how far the fall speed exceeds the threshold, capped at a maximum. Light landings and normal walking trigger no shake.
7. Expose the threshold, max strength, duration, and smoothing values as exported variables so they can be tuned in the editor without touching code. Respect an optional setting to disable shake for accessibility.
8. Playtest level_01 by dropping from several heights, checking that small hops stay calm, big falls shake proportionally, the camera stays within limits, and the enemies and collisions are unaffected.
